problem_text:
An engineering firm must dispatch a field inspector to evaluate eight critical infrastructure sites across a region.  
The sites are positioned at these grid coordinates (in miles):  

Site Alpha: (8,146)  
Site Beta: (23,173)  
Site Gamma: (132,194)  
Site Delta: (153,19)  
Site Epsilon: (191,109)  
Site Zeta: (193,52)  
Site Eta: (74,137)  
Site Theta: (153,106)  

Travel distances between sites are as follows (in miles):  
Alpha to Gamma: 133.0  
Alpha to Delta: 192.8  
Alpha to Epsilon: 186.7  
Alpha to Zeta: 207.5  
Alpha to Eta: 66.6  
Alpha to Theta: 150.4  
Beta to Gamma: 111.0  
Beta to Delta: 201.5  
Beta to Epsilon: 179.8  
Beta to Zeta: 208.7  
Beta to Eta: 62.4  
Beta to Theta: 146.2  
Gamma to Delta: 176.3  
Gamma to Epsilon: 103.5  
Gamma to Zeta: 154.5  
Gamma to Eta: 81.3  
Gamma to Theta: 90.5  
Delta to Epsilon: 97.7  
Delta to Zeta: 51.9  
Delta to Eta: 142.0  
Delta to Theta: 87.0  
Epsilon to Zeta: 57.0  
Epsilon to Eta: 120.3  
Epsilon to Theta: 38.1  
Zeta to Eta: 146.2  
Zeta to Theta: 67.2  
Eta to Theta: 84.9  

Due to terrain restrictions, there is no direct route connecting Site Alpha and Site Beta.  
Furthermore, owing to scheduling and access limitations, exactly one of the following two inspection segments must be incorporated into the circuit: the route between Site Beta and Site Gamma, or the route between Site Gamma and Site Delta.  

The objective is to determine the most efficient inspection tour that visits every site precisely once, begins and ends at the same location, and minimizes the total travel distance.
